reading.body:
Liam Anderson is disclosed as a lobbyist on five AI-related filings, all for one client, the AI Policy Network, and all naming bills from 2025 or later.

The pattern is narrow and concentrated. One lobbyist, one client, five filings, and eighteen bills listed across them. The prior government positions disclosed are all congressional and executive branch staff roles, including communications director for two House members, staff for another, and staff at the Department of Health and Human Services. That is the background the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to report from the previous twenty years.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative layer of the buildout, not the compute layer. The bills named here are where AI policy is being written, and the people writing it are former congressional and agency staff. The data does not say what any of these bills would do, whether they passed, or what position the client took. It also does not say how much was spent, what was discussed in any meeting, or whether the lobbying had any effect. It records who filed, for whom, and which bills were named.

The page covers one lobbyist and one client. It does not establish that this activity is unusual, and it draws no conclusion about the person.
